segments.text: Betelgeuse is the red star on Orion's shoulder. You can see it tonight with your own eyes.
segments.headline: Orion's red shoulder

segments.text: It's about seven hundred times wider than our Sun. In our solar system, it would reach past Mars.
In twenty nineteen, it suddenly dimmed, and people wondered if it was about to explode. It turned out to be a giant cloud of dust it had thrown off.
segments.headline: The Great Dimming

segments.text: And in twenty twenty-five, astronomers finally spotted a small companion star circling it, named Siwarha, meaning her bracelet.
segments.headline: A hidden companion: Siwarha

segments.text: Within about a hundred thousand years, it will explode as a supernova, bright enough to see in daylight.
